docs.title: sparky.house homelab
docs.text:
These are the build and re-install notes for the homelab behind sparky.house: a small rack of network gear, a few servers, and the services they run.

These notes are mainly for me. Some pages are well tested and some aren't, so check each step against your own setup before you run it.

Most details are private

This copy has the outline only. Addresses, hostnames, software, versions, and how things are reached or secured are in a password-protected copy.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
• Network: how the network is laid out and reached.
  • Hosts: one page per machine, with what it runs and how to rebuild it.
  • Apps: every service in the lab.
  • Home automation: the smart-home hub and what connects to it.
  • Monitoring: uptime checks, the dashboard, and host metrics.
  • Operations: updates, backups, and problems I hit more than once.

docs.title: Build this site locally
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve -a 0.0.0.0:8000

Then open http://localhost:8000, or port 8000 on your machine's LAN address from a phone. That preview hides private details. To see everything without a password on your own machine, run HOMELAB_PUBLIC=false mkdocs serve -a 0.0.0.0:8000.

docs.title: Private details
docs.text:
The site builds twice from the same pages:

Build Where Shows Public The site root An outline: page titles, one-line summaries, and this page Private /private/ Everything, with every page encrypted by one password

docs.title: What goes where
docs.text:
Three rules decide where a detail goes:

  • Public: only what can't help anyone break in. That means what the lab is for, the outline of these notes, and how the two copies work.
  • Private: anything that helps an attacker reach, identify, or get into a host or a service. That covers addresses, hostnames, ports, which software runs where and at what version, how each thing is reached and signed in to, user names, update habits, backup gaps, and known weaknesses.
  • Nowhere: personal data, secrets, and account identifiers. That covers the WAN address, email addresses, MAC addresses, people's names, room-by-room device lists, passwords and tokens, and tunnel, account, or zone IDs. These stay out of the repo entirely, private blocks included, and tools/leakcheck.py fails CI if one shows up.

Page titles, nav labels, and URLs aren't encrypted in either copy, so they stay generic: "Proxy host", not the host's name.

docs.title: Mark a page or a block private
docs.text:
Most pages are private as a whole. Put this front matter at the top, and the public copy shows only the title and the summary:

---
private: true
public_summary: One sentence that gives nothing away.
---

On a public page, wrap private details in a private admonition. Everything indented under the marker belongs to the block:

!!! private "Addresses"
    | Host | Address |
    | ---- | ------- |
    | example-host | EXAMPLE_ADDRESS |

Use ??? private for a block that starts collapsed. For a note that belongs only on the public site, such as a pointer to the private copy, use !!! public.

To preview everything on your own machine without a password, run:

HOMELAB_PUBLIC=false mkdocs serve -a 0.0.0.0:8000

docs.title: Add a diagram
docs.text:
Architecture diagrams come from the IcePanel model of the lab, exported as PNG files into diagrams/ at the top of the repo, outside docs/. On a private page, reference one like this:

![What the diagram shows](diagram:context.png)

The private build embeds the image inside the page, so it's encrypted with everything else. Readers can click it to open it full size. A diagram image never becomes its own file on the site, because an image file would be readable without the password. The build fails if a public page references a diagram, and tools/leakcheck.py fails if any image file appears under docs/.

docs.title: How the protection works
docs.text:
The encryptcontent plugin encrypts each private page with AES-256. The key comes from the password through PBKDF2 with 1,000,000 rounds. Your browser decrypts the page, and it keeps the key for the rest of the session, so you enter the password once.

Keep these limits in mind:

  • The encrypted pages are public files. Anyone can download them and try passwords offline, so use a long, random password.
  • Page titles, the navigation, and URLs aren't encrypted. Keep private details out of page titles, file names, and mkdocs.yml.
  • Changing the password doesn't protect copies someone already downloaded.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
CI runs these checks before anything deploys:

  1. tools/leakcheck.py fails on personal data or account IDs in any page.
  2. The private build fails if DOCS_PASSWORD is missing or shorter than 16 characters.
  3. tools/privatecheck.py fails if private text is readable in the public site, or unencrypted anywhere in the private one. On the public site it also fails on any IP address or sparky.house subdomain, wherever it came from.
